rejected.title: Modern art and culture
card: Modern artists broke from realistic styles to show a changed and unsettled world. This break began before the First World War and grew after 1918, as new film and jazz also reflected the modern age.
Expressionism
began in Germany around 1905. It shows strong feelings through distorted shapes and bold colours, rather than a true-to-life picture.
Cubism
began around 1907 with Pablo Picasso and Georges Braque. It breaks objects into shapes and shows them from several angles at once.
Surrealism
began in 1924, between the wars. It draws on dreams and the unconscious mind to create strange, dreamlike images.
rejected.remember: Modern art broke from realism, starting before 1914 and growing after the war.

a.q: An artist paints an ordinary room where objects float and melt, as in a dream. Which movement does this match?
a.why: Dreamlike scenes that draw on the unconscious mind are the mark of Surrealism. Expressionism also distorts things, but it does so to show strong feeling, not to create a dream world.

b.q: A painting shows a violin as flat shapes, seen from the front and the side at the same time. Which movement does it best match?
b.why: Showing an object from several angles at once as broken shapes is the mark of Cubism. Expressionism distorts shapes too, but its aim is to show emotion, and Surrealism draws on dreams.
b.clue: Look at how the object is shown from different angles.

draft.title: Modern art and culture
card: After the First World War, many artists broke from realistic styles. They tried new ways to show a changed and unsettled world.
Expressionism
shows strong feelings through distorted shapes and bold colours, rather than a true-to-life picture.
Cubism
breaks objects into shapes and shows them from several angles at once. Pablo Picasso was a leading Cubist.
Surrealism
draws on dreams and the unconscious mind to create strange, dreamlike images. New film and jazz music also reflected and shaped the modern age.
draft.remember: Modern art and culture broke from realism to express a changing world.

a.q: Which art movement drew on dreams and the unconscious mind?
a.why: Surrealism used dreams to create strange images. Expressionism shows strong feeling through distortion, and Cubism breaks objects into shapes seen from several angles.

b.q: A painting shows a violin as flat shapes, seen from the front and the side at the same time. Which movement does it best match?
b.why: Showing an object from several angles as broken shapes is the mark of Cubism. Expressionism focuses on emotion, and Surrealism on dreams.
b.clue: Look at how the object is shown from different angles.

problems.detail: The card opens with 'After the First World War, many artists broke from realistic styles' and then lists Expressionism and Cubism, which implies both began after the war. Expressionism (about 1905) and Cubism (about 1907–08, Picasso and Braque) began before the First World War. Only Surrealism (1924) arose between the wars. The card should say these movements began before or after the war, or that the break from realism started earlier and grew after 1918.
